series_definition.name: Frontier cost to LEO
series_definition.description: The lowest publicly-available list price per kg to LEO in each anchor year. This is the FRONTIER, not an industry average and not a transacted average. Points are anchored to the arrival of a vehicle that reset the frontier.
series_definition.units: nominal USD per kilogram to Low Earth Orbit
series_definition.dollar_basis: nominal USD of each point's price_year, which is NOT its anchor year. The 1981 Shuttle figure, for example, is quoted in 2008 dollars. Deflate with price_year, never with year.
series_definition.real_series: Real values are not stored here. Use cost_to_orbit.analysis.to_real() with data/deflator.json to deflate, so the deflator is explicit and auditable rather than baked into the data.
caveats: The frontier is what the cheapest vehicle would charge at maximum expendable payload. Almost no customer buys that. See the falcon-9-rideshare row in vehicles.json for what a small customer actually pays.
Pre-2010 points mix program-cost and list-price bases. They are not strictly comparable to the post-2010 points and are marked with lower confidence.
Nominal. In real terms the decline is steeper before 2018 and the post-2018 flattening is a real-terms decline.
year is when the vehicle reset the frontier; price_year is the dollar basis of the figure. Conflating the two overstates the real decline by a factor of more than two at the 1981 peak.

points.note: Inflation-adjusted program cost per launch over 140 t payload. Contested; estimates span roughly $6,300-8,800/kg.
Program cost per flight in 2008 USD over 27.5 t payload. The frontier moved backwards: reusability without cheap refurbishment.
EELV-era expendable frontier. Price figure is 2016 reported cost applied to the 2006 debut, so this point is dated later than its anchor year.
Derived: ~$54M list over 10,450 kg LEO. SpaceX enters and undercuts incumbents on expendable pricing alone, before reuse.
Derived: ~$90M debut list price over 63,800 kg. Falcon 9 Block 5 in the same year was ~$2,719/kg at a $62M list price.
Derived: $97M list over 63,800 kg. The nominal frontier has RISEN since 2018 as SpaceX raised list prices for inflation. No competitor has undercut it.
